title: Spike by Ian Hislop & Nick Newman - review & photos - Watermill & UK Tour
transcript: hello and welcome to one minute theater reviews i'm paul seven lewis and i'm here at the wonderful water move theater in newbury to see spike spike by nick newman and ian hislop is clearly a labor of love spike milligan had a long association with private eye magazine and the authors both from private eye clearly feel great affection for him however to succeed spike faced three challenges firstly i'm not sure that many people under 60 will know about spike milligan or remember the groon show if phrases like you dirty rotten swine you're dead at me again or i fell into water leave you scratching your head that probably proves my point secondly the actors couldn't hope to recreate the geniuses that were milligan peter sellers and harry seeker they don't try and instead their characters stand at a slight distance from the originals giving us an objective insight into this comedy legend that's interesting but not as funny finally how to convey milligan's anarchic spirit which was very much a product of his mental state again it's an excellent observation of him but the play doesn't get inside him that's the one minute review but keep watching for more about spike including what worked and didn't work what was especially funny that wasn't anything to do with spike milligan and what the clever set was like if you are one of those people who doesn't know about spike milligan let me explain he was a brilliant comic writer and performer best known as the writer of the goon show the trouble is the last goon show to be transmitted on the bbc home service was back in 1960 with a couple of tv specials over the next decade or so it was his surrealist and absurd humor that made the goon show a phenomenal hit take this brief example [Music] what time is it taker oh just a minute i i got it written down here on a piece of paper milligan was an acknowledged influence on future comedies and comics including monty python and eddie izzard after the goons milligan continued to pour out anarchic humor he wrote poetry plays and books and appeared a number of tv programs throughout the 70s and 80s he died in 2002 but the goon show is still what is best known for and that's what this play concentrates on we see the early resistance from the bbc to the show's revolutionary and rebellious style to the show becoming hugely popular we also learn about spike's difficult personal life his traumatic experience as a soldier in the second world war and his mental illness and how the pressure of writing the goon show took its toll and here's the other challenge the actors playing milligan and his fella goons peter sellers and harry secum cannot hope to recreate their genius their their voices their timing their understanding of each other the way they perform as if they've just read the script and are enjoying it as much as the audience sensibly the cast don't try to do impressions of the originals instead they act out their own interpretation of these characters which makes it an interesting story but not anything like as funny as you might expect the jokes are there of course particularly milligan's plays on words a sign on his door says do not disturb i'm disturbed enough already but they cannot hope to deliver them with the power of the actual goons the voices can never be quite as ridiculous the irony never quite as sharp and i'm not in any way denigrating the actors john deglish's milligan is an excellent comic actor with a great plasticine face and he plays his part with verve giving a strong impression of a man on the edge george kemp's sellers and jeremy lloyd to seek and provide excellent support robert mountford represents the stiff voice of authority very well the story of tortured comic genius is familiar as is that of an artist rebelling against and rejected by the establishment and still until following success the establishment finally embraces him but it's still a story worth telling to beef up the laughs the writers cleverly weave in an almost discreet story about sound effects now these effects are an important part of the goon show and although i said it was nothing to do with spike milligan he was the one who set the challenge to the sound effects people and margaret cabone smith humorously explains how they were achieved at various points during the play i think with nothing to compare this gets the biggest response from the audience director paul hart who is the water mills artistic director keeps up a good pace so you won't be bored and katie lyres helps by keeping a set design simple the stage represents a recording studio that with minimal changes converts to various offices a battleground a pub and spike's home she uses the backs of the stage well i mean often there's uh there are milliganish cartoons telling us the location of the scene and projections higher suggests the state of milligan's mind and there's the third challenge in a play mainly about milligan's mental state how do you convey it yes john deglish sparks and crumples and yes the play uh the story tells us how in his mind this battle with army officers becomes a battle with the bbc authorities this is interesting and fun but rather plodding in a way that milligan would never have been uh as is suggested by the cover of the programme as a tribute to spike milligan maybe nick newman and ian hislock needed to inject their play with more of their heroes anarchic spirit i still enjoyed it and i give spike three stars i hope you found this review interesting uh if you did and you want to know about my future reviews please subscribe by clicking on the link below and if you want to read my reviews go to oneminutetheatreviews.co.uk thank you for watching
